title: AI inquiry urges data centre action
full_text:
A bipartisan parliamentary inquiry into artificial intelligence has taken the unprecedented step of writing to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, urging the government to invest in data centres for the national interest and insist independent assessors are given high-level access to model developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic to monitor their activities in real time.
The committee has also given the Albanese government approval to press ahead with changes to copyright laws that will make it easier for major AI developers to train their models in local data centres.
The inquiry, chaired by Labor MP Jo Briskey, has been examining the rapid growth of AI use in Australia, calling data centre developers and regulators alongside the biggest companies in the sector: OpenAI and Anthropic, which have built the popular ChatGPT and Claude models respectively.
In a letter to Albanese co-signed by Brinskey and Liberal senator Jonno Duniam, extracts of which have been seen by The Australian Financial Review, the committee says the "fast-changing nature of AI" and the "urgent need" for safeguards meant that it was necessary to provide an early indication of the inquiry's recommendations to inform the government's work.
Among the broader recommendations is a push for the government to invest directly in computing power, or data centres where AI is processed.
